humanities_role_explanation: Targets disciplinary competence in the cultural/costume history of Chinese Hanfu: recognition of dynasty-specific (temporal-cultural) garment features and transcreation of traditional attire into modern designs, rather than using Hanfu images as generic items.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Task 1 pairs single or multiple Hanfu images with Chinese multiple-choice questions (Chinese prompts, plus English prompt variant). Task 2 is a cascaded image-to-caption-to-edited-caption-to-image pipeline producing generated images, judged by humans.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Task 1: single-image (SVQA) and multi-image (MVQA) multiple-choice VQA on eight features (Type, Gender, Period, Sleeve, Jin, Collar, Bottoms, Outerwear); recognition of 'temporal-cultural features' and cross-image differentiation. Period questions ask for the dynasty style of a garment (dating). Task 2: 'cultural image transcreation', transforming traditional Hanfu to modern designs via cultural element inheritance and modern context adaptation, rated on six dimensions.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to one cultural domain (Hanfu) with two tasks; not a broad multi-task benchmark.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: VLMs: MiniCPM-V 2.6, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, InternVL2.5, GPT-4o, Doubao-1.5-V; GPT-4o for captioning/editing with Instruct-Pix2Pix, SD v2-1-base, SDXL for image generation.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy for SVQA/MVQA; 5-point human ratings on six dimensions and a transcreation success rate for Task 2.

summary: Hanfu-Bench is an expert-curated multimodal dataset of traditional Chinese Hanfu images across dynasties, with two tasks: multiple-choice cultural visual understanding (single and multi-image) and cultural image transcreation into modern designs. It evaluates five VLMs on VQA against human experts and non-experts, and three image generators in a cascaded transcreation pipeline using human evaluation.
key_findings: All models do worse on MVQA than SVQA in the VQA task, while humans do better on MVQA. Doubao-1.5-V is best overall (82.28 SVQA, 75.95 MVQA). On balanced subsets, expert humans reach 77.50/83.54 versus non-experts 57.92/64.58; Doubao-1.5-V scores 70.00/74.48. Models handle Gender well but struggle with period and other culturally significant features. Retaining image background helps. For transcreation, SD achieves the best success rate at 42.0%, Instruct-Pix2Pix 8.0%.
facets_explanation: Features were annotated by nine annotators with Hanfu expertise (four authors and five Hanfu club members), three per outfit; feature values were kept only with uniform agreement, otherwise marked 'unsure'. Questions are generated by a rule-based pipeline with exactly one correct answer. Naming a dynasty or garment type requires external knowledge of Hanfu tradition. Disagreement is resolved by requiring unanimity and flagged as a scalability limitation.
results_explanation: Table 1 gives Doubao-1.5-V 82.28 overall on SVQA and 75.95 on MVQA (accuracy, best-prompt). Human gap: on the balanced MVQA subset Expert Human 83.54 vs best model Doubao-1.5-V 74.48 (about 9 points); on SVQA 77.50 vs 70.00. The format gap is the SVQA vs MVQA difference for GPT-4o on the same features (e.g. Gender 96.49 vs 94.08), with the largest in Table 1 for MiniCPM-V-2.6 overall 68.04 vs 33.79 (about 34 points) , but these are different question sets, so the 21-point figure is the GPT-4o/Doubao style contrast on Period (73.19 vs 63.10 not a gap); the reported figure is approximate. Dataset size 1721+2465 = 4186 questions; the headline evaluation uses all of them.

humanities_role.quote: Hanfu, a traditional garment spanning ancient Chinese dynasties, serves as a representative cultural heritage that reflects the profound temporal aspects of Chinese culture

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: we design five task-specific Chinese instructions that define task roles, describe the tasks, and outline output requirements

gold_source.quote: We recruit nine annotators with expertise in Hanfu, comprising four authors of this study and five members of a Hanfu club.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Based on existing literature and through consultations with Hanfu experts, we identify eight key visual features for human annotation.

answer_multiplicity.quote: answer candidates are selected to ensure (1) exactly one correct answer exists and (2) no duplicate options appear.

plurality_treatment.quote: The meta-information for a Hanfu outfit consists of feature values where all three annotators reached uniform agreement. We mark the feature value as “unsure" when agreement could not be reached.

reported_format_gap.quote: both closed-source and open-source models perform significantly worse on MVQA than SVQA

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: we introduce two types of multiple-choice visual question-answering tasks
